title: adaptive-drip-reserve: reduce starvation under skew while preserving latency SLOs
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive drip-reserve scheduler mode to improve fairness and avoid KV-cache starvation under heavy skew. No API changes. Enable via runtime.scheduler.mode=adaptive-drip-reserve in config.
description:
Context: production canaries exposed a starvation pattern for low-weight tenants and short-context requests when high-KV-pin, long-context requests dominated the continuous-batcher. Existing slot-reservations prevented throughput collapse but caused long-tail latency for small requests and frequent timeouts. Motivation: reduce starvation and p95/p99 tail for short requests while keeping throughput and aggregate cost similar.

Design summary: This PR introduces an 'adaptive drip reserve' scheduler mode implemented in the runtime scheduler. Key ideas: 1) Maintain a small per-priority 'reserve' that slowly leaks tokens (a drip) back into the ready pool on a tunable cadence; 2) Decay soft-reservations for idle priorities using an exponential backoff so long-running heavy partitions can't permanently hold slots; 3) Add jittered short timeouts on reserve probes to avoid synchronized bursts; 4) Add a KV-pin-aware admission heuristic that treats requests with high KV cache pressure differently (short-circuit to larger model variant or enqueue with higher backpressure).

Operator knobs added: runtime.scheduler.adaptive_drip.enabled (bool), .base_drip_ms (int, default 6), .max_reserve_fraction (float, default 0.12), .idle_decay_ms (int, default 250), .kv_pin_backoff_threshold (int, default 32).

Compatibility: default scheduler remains unchanged. New mode must be opted-in per-cluster. No external API or protocol changes.

Benchmarks and canary results: Microbench (small seq=32) on n1-gpu cluster: p95 latency reduced by 11.7% and p99 by 9.3% under 75% util skewed workload. End-to-end throughput for mixed workload changed by -1.8% (within noise). KV-starvation simulation test shows median fairness index (Jain) improved from 0.62 to 0.84. Canary in us-west-2 (10% traffic) ran for 72h with no increase in 5xx and with a single flaky integration test that was identified as unrelated to scheduling.

Implementation notes: core scheduler logic in src/runtime/scheduler/drip_reserve.rs. Added a lightweight state machine that tracks per-priority reserve tokens and a jittered drip timer. The admission heuristic consults the KV cache estimator (src/runtime/kv/kv_estimator.rs) and uses a conservative backoff flag for requests exceeding kv_pin_backoff_threshold. Changes are guarded behind a feature flag and config checks for easy rollback. A new deterministic unit test harness (src/runtime/tests/scheduler_drip_sim.rs) simulates adversarial arrival patterns to validate no starvation within 10k simulated slots.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed offline with SRE and runtime team - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Canaryed on staging and us-west-2 - [x] Feature flag + config switch - [x] Metrics and dashboards updated (see observability note)

Observability: added metrics runtime.scheduler.reserve_tokens{priority,cluster}, runtime.scheduler.drip_events_total, runtime.scheduler.reserve_evictions_total. Grafana dashboard rows updated for per-priority tail latency and reserve utilization. Suggest alerting on reserve_evictions_total > 20/min as a regression signal.

Rollback plan: flip runtime.scheduler.adaptive_drip.enabled=false and/or revert config to main scheduler; draining rollout via canary.

Notes: The algorithm was intentionally conservative; we expect further follow-ups to tune decay windows per-customer and to explore integration with request-level QoS hints (future work: ENG-4310).

review_comments: Eliot Chang: Overall this is a great direction. Two concerns: 1) spillover interaction with current autoscaler — do we risk oscillations? 2) Need clearer invariants for reserve_evictions_total so SRE can alert reliably.

Maya Patel (author): Autoscaler interactions addressed by adding a conservative upper bound max_reserve_fraction and by ensuring drip only returns it's own tokens not capacity we allocate from autoscaler. I added a note in the design doc and an integration test to exercise scale-down scenarios.
Soraya Ahmed: Can we make the base_drip_ms configurable per-priority in the future? Some tenants are very latency-sensitive.
Maya Patel: Yes—added a follow-up TODO and linked ENG-4310 for per-tenant windows. Kept defaults cluster-wide for this PR to reduce rollout complexity.
Jonas Ruiz: The kv_pin_backoff_threshold default seems aggressive for larger KV footprints; please show sensitivity matrix.
Maya Patel: Added sensitivity table in the PR description and committed a test that varies the threshold; results in docs/ops updated.
Eliot Chang (approver): Verified canary dashboards and unit tests. Approve.
